title: Current practices and future direction of artificial intelligence in mathematics education: A systematic review
venue: International Electronic Journal of Mathematics Education
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the need for a practical and up-to-date synthesis of how artificial intelligence is being used in mathematics education. The authors argue that prior reviews often focused on broad AI categories or research-stage systems, but gave less attention to specific, market-ready tools that educators could actually implement. The review therefore asks four main questions: how AI in mathematics education studies are distributed across educational levels, what AI tools are used and how they can be categorized, which commercialized tools are available online and what they do, and what emerging trends and future directions appear in the literature.

The study uses a systematic literature review approach. The authors searched Web of Science and Scopus for English-language journal articles published between 2019 and 2024, focused on AI in mathematics education. After screening and deduplication, 32 studies were included. The review categorizes AI tools into adaptive learning systems/intelligent tutoring systems, chatbots, augmented reality, virtual reality, learning analytics, serious games, and AI mathematics problem solvers. It also identifies named tools such as Khan Academy, Squirrel AI, ChatGPT, Bard, GeoGebra, GeoGebra AR, Photomath, Vuforia, and NeoTrieVR, and distinguishes between generative AI tools and pedagogical AI tools.

The population represented across the reviewed studies spans primary/elementary, middle/high school, university, and adult learners, with the largest share of studies at the middle/high school level, followed by university/adult and then primary levels. Because this is a review, the context is not one single intervention site but a synthesis of studies conducted across multiple countries, with especially strong representation from China, the United States, and Spain. The paper is situated in mathematics education broadly and examines both classroom-oriented and digital learning applications of AI.

The main conclusions are that AI in mathematics education is expanding rapidly and serves multiple instructional purposes, especially personalization, adaptive feedback, interactive visualization, and problem support. Chatbots were the most common category in recent studies, while AR/VR showed strong promise for engagement and conceptual understanding, especially for geometry and spatial learning. The authors conclude that commercialized pedagogical AI tools currently dominate the field, but generative AI tools are increasingly important. They also emphasize the need for more longitudinal research, stronger understanding of long-term effects and equity implications, and more work on how AI can complement rather than replace teachers.

identified_tools.name: ITS (General)
identified_tools.description: Intelligent tutoring systems and adaptive learning systems used in mathematics education to provide personalized instruction, adaptive feedback, and tailored problem-solving support.
identified_tools.use_case: This systematic review synthesizes studies of ITS/adaptive learning tools in mathematics education and discusses examples such as ALEKS, MATHia, PAT2Math, GeoGebra Tutor, MathE, Squirrel AI, and Khan Academy as part of the broader AIME landscape.

findings.finding_summary: The review reports that adaptive learning systems and intelligent tutoring systems were identified in prior literature as significantly enhancing elementary students' mathematics achievement, particularly through personalized learning experiences and adaptive feedback. In this paper's own synthesis, these tools are described as attracting significant attention for their effectiveness in providing personalized learning experiences and tailored feedback, but no pooled effect size, confidence interval, or aggregate sample is reported.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generative AI tools and general AI chatbots used to generate explanations, step-by-step solutions, and conversational assistance in mathematics education.
identified_tools.use_case: The review discusses generative AI platforms in mathematics education broadly and categorizes tools such as ChatGPT, Bard, and Photomath as commercialized AIME tools used for math explanations and problem solving.

findings.finding_summary: The review identifies generative AI tools as useful for instant assistance with solving mathematical problems and for generating personalized explanations of complex concepts. It also notes AI-driven analytics and feedback systems, including chatbots, as improving learning outcomes through real-time personalized support, though no pooled quantitative estimate is reported.
findings.measure: mathematics learning outcomes/problem-solving support in reviewed studies

identified_tools.name: Mobile Learning Apps (General)
identified_tools.description: AR/VR-based and mobile mathematics learning applications that support visualization, interaction, and immersive exploration of mathematical concepts.
identified_tools.use_case: The review synthesizes studies of augmented reality, virtual reality, and related mathematics applications such as GeoGebra AR, cleARmaths, Vuforia, CalcVR, NeoTrieVR, and mobile math trails tools.

findings.finding_summary: The thematic synthesis reports that AR and VR technologies in mathematics education show promising results for enhancing students' motivation and problem-solving skills, and for making abstract concepts more engaging and tangible. The discussion further states that AR/VR tools are especially suited for explaining geometric concepts, but no effect sizes or aggregate sample sizes are provided.
findings.measure: motivation, problem-solving skills, and understanding of mathematical concepts in reviewed studies

quality_tier_rationale: This is a systematic review of 32 studies with a clear search and screening process, but it is not a meta-analysis and does not provide pooled quantitative estimates or detailed risk-of-bias assessment for tool-specific outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: The review consistently reports positive effects across AI categories in mathematics education, but impact magnitude is unclear because no pooled effect sizes or confidence intervals are reported.
